results.content: If rapid, accurate, and affordable point of care of testing for GBS colonization could be developed to optimize the administration of IAP, this would minimize GBS transmission risk and greatly improve the disease burden in LMICs. In light of this, we evaluated the diagnostic performance of the HiberGene (HG) GBS loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay for the detection of maternal GBS rectovaginal colonization, comparing it to enrichment culture using the World Health Organization criteria for diagnostic test suitability [11]. This is the first study to investigate rapid diagnostic tests in labor for the assessment of GBS rectovaginal colonization in Uganda and the first to indicate acceptable sensitivity and specificity of the HG GBS LAMP assay, compared to culture, regardless of a pre-enrichment step. For direct swab testing, similar sensitivity results were reported in a prior study evaluating diagnostic accuracy the HG GBS LAMP assay in Ireland (92.2%) [14], as well as other studies evaluating rapid molecular-based assays, including the GeneOhm IDI-strep B (91.1%) [17] and quantitative PCR (95.5%) [18].
